name: Comeback Kid
label: Victory
lede: Two guitarists in a Winnipeg Christian hardcore band started a side project named for a Mario Lemieux headline. Then one of them walked up to the microphone and stayed there.

eras.title: A side project with a hockey headline for a name
eras.text: Andrew Neufeld and Jeremy Hiebert were playing guitar in Figure Four when they started Comeback Kid on the side in 2001, borrowing the name from a newspaper headline about Mario Lemieux returning to the NHL. Two years later the side project had a debut album out.

years.h: Figure Four's two guitarists start a band named for Mario Lemieux
years.p: Andrew Neufeld and Jeremy Hiebert recruit singer Scott Wade and drummer Kyle Profeta in Winnipeg. Lemieux had come out of retirement three months earlier.
years.xp:
Comeback Kid began in March 2001 as a side project while Neufeld and Hiebert were still in the Christian hardcore band Figure Four. Neufeld and Hiebert played guitar; Wade sang.

Wikipedia credits the name to a newspaper headline about Lemieux, the Pittsburgh Penguins star who came out of retirement in December 2000.

years.h: Six songs on a demo
years.p: It is Comeback Kid's first recording, released seven months before the band signs with a label.

years.h: California's Facedown Records signs a Winnipeg band
years.p: Comeback Kid goes into the studio for its first album in November 2002, three months later.

years.h: Turn It Around crams 13 songs into 28 minutes
years.p: Comeback Kid's Facedown debut has Scott Wade singing and Cliff Heide on bass. Give Me Strength presses the vinyl, and the band tours full time afterward.
years.xp: The album was recorded in November 2002. It is Comeback Kid's first full-length, released March 4, 2003, and the 28-minute running time covers all 13 songs.

eras.title: Thirteen days at the Blasting Room
eras.text: For its second album the band went to Fort Collins, Colorado, to work with Bill Stevenson of the Descendents. Wake the Dead came out on Victory Records and turned a Winnipeg side project into a band hardcore kids sing back at every show.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wake the Dead · Wikipedia: Comeback Kid
years.h: [[Bill Stevenson|328e3ae5-7d8c-4a01-b2b3-b8f41fb7bb23]] cuts Wake the Dead in 13 days
years.p: Stevenson and Jason Livermore record the second album at the Blasting Room in Fort Collins. It reaches No. 16 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.
years.xp:
The 11 songs run 25 minutes, 46 seconds, and the album also reaches No. 27 on Top Independent Albums. [[Russ Rankin|99fd5943-758d-4c1b-bd2c-4b6d0d1e037a]] of [[Good Riddance|ab4725b8-7a2f-429a-a55a-3dde07c9acea]] sings on Our Distance, and Luke Friesen is among those adding vocals to the title track. It is Scott Wade's last album as the band's singer.

Wikipedia's album page lists Smallman as the label (catalog SMR 026); Wikipedia's band page credits Victory Records.

years.h: Burnout Revenge and Burnout Legends both play the title track
years.p: EA puts Wake the Dead on the soundtracks of its two racing games.

eras.title: The guitarist takes the microphone
eras.text: Scott Wade left after Wake the Dead, and the band skipped auditions: guitarist Andrew Neufeld became the singer. Broadcasting... showed it worked, and two years on the road across North America and Europe followed.

years.cap: Comeback Kid on stage in Münster, Germany, 2006
years.src: Wikipedia: Comeback Kid · Wikipedia: Die Knowing
years.h: Scott Wade quits, and Andrew Neufeld moves from guitar to the mic
years.p: Wade leaves after Wake the Dead. Neufeld, a co-founder, goes from rhythm guitar to lead vocals.
years.xp: Wade stayed friendly with the band. He sang guest vocals on [[Silverstein|d89de379-665d-425c-b2e9-41b95d1edb36]]'s A Shipwreck in the Sand in 2009, and came back for Full Swing on Die Knowing in 2014.

years.h: Neufeld's first album as singer, Broadcasting...
years.p: Back at the Blasting Room with Bill Stevenson in November 2006, Comeback Kid makes a record that reaches No. 3 on Heatseekers and No. 129 on the Billboard 200. The title track ends up in NHL 2K8.

years.h: Tours with [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]], then Europe with [[Parkway Drive|a436dd02-0549-4c91-b608-df451217fdeb]]
years.p: The European run is the Never Say Die tour. The band takes a short break at the end of 2007.

years.h: Bassist Kevin Call leaves on good terms, and Matt Keil steps in
years.p: Call played bass on Wake the Dead and Broadcasting....

years.h: Through the Noise looks back at six years on CD and DVD
years.p: The live release includes a set recorded in Leipzig, Germany in fall 2007.

eras.title: Distort at home, Victory abroad, and a drummer's exit
eras.text: Comeback Kid moved to Distort in Canada and stayed with Victory Records for the US. Two more albums came out on Victory before the founding drummer left to cook in South Africa.

years.h: Symptoms + Cures: Distort in Canada, Victory in the US
years.p: Comeback Kid's fourth album is made in Toronto with producers Eric Ratz and Kenny Luong. Members of [[Cancer Bats|00b952be-6c97-4880-84f9-06de584b491b]], [[A Wilhelm Scream|657ec972-3ab1-48a8-b472-1f1c210aaf17]] and Architects guest.

years.h: A van accident with Gravemaker turns into a Comeback Kid song
years.p: Andrew Neufeld was in the accident; according to Wikipedia it inspired G.M. Vincent and I.

years.h: Stu Ross of [[Misery Signals|0b0b523f-e9d5-4f18-919c-ebf084a58c26]] replaces Casey Hjelmberg on guitar
years.p: Hjelmberg announces in early 2012 that he is leaving. Ross also played in Living with Lions.

years.cap: Comeback Kid at Vainstream Rockfest, July 2014
years.h: Die Knowing is the last Comeback Kid album on Victory
years.p: Kyle Black produces, and Should Know Better is the single. Original singer Scott Wade comes back as a guest on Full Swing.

years.h: Kyle Profeta, drummer since day one, is off to cook in South Africa
years.p: Comeback Kid's drummer since 2001 announces he is leaving to focus on his culinary skills.

eras.title: Twenty years of Wake the Dead
eras.text: Comeback Kid moved to Nuclear Blast and kept releasing records, and the biggest moment in every set is still a song from 2005. In 2025 the band toured Wake the Dead in full and lost a former bassist to ALS.

years.cap: Comeback Kid at Impericon Festival, Oberhausen
years.h: Outsider is the first Comeback Kid album after Victory
years.p: The metal label Nuclear Blast releases the sixth album worldwide.

years.cap: Comeback Kid at Full Force, June 2022
years.h: Two labels share Heavy Steps
years.p: Comeback Kid's seventh album is on New Damage in Canada and Nuclear Blast everywhere else.

years.h: The Trouble EP lands on SharpTone Records
years.p: It follows Heavy Steps by two years.

years.big: "the biggest moment in every single set that we've played"
years.src: Wikipedia: Wake the Dead · Wikipedia: Comeback Kid
years.h: Comeback Kid plays Wake the Dead in full for its 20th
years.p: Andrew Neufeld on the title track. The band tours the US, then Canada in September, and re-records the song.
years.xp:
Neufeld said the song lands hardest in every set the band plays, from Asia and South America to Europe, Africa and North America.

The 20th anniversary shows play the album start to finish.

years.h: Former bassist Matt Keil dies of ALS
years.p: Keil took over bass in late 2007 and played on Die Knowing. Wikipedia reports he died in July 2025.
